**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb71296c3fbf0c24a95df09c7a64f503189ef5c5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `65586da9d8c2b9251d9059cc4ee02a459c12982a` — the merge of head `dc36df3226b388498826f21073f9ac2a0cbb3cec` into base `fb71296c3fbf0c24a95df09c7a64f503189ef5c5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

git fetch origin 65586da9d8c2b9251d9059cc4ee02a459c12982a && git checkout 65586da9d8c2b9251d9059cc4ee02a459c12982a

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc36df3226b388498826f21073f9ac2a0cbb3cec`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/canonicalize-stored-flow.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-label-on-result.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-node-config-values-at-registration.dogfood.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx

Rendered 2026-11-10T16:24Z by an isolated sub-agent of this seat at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, from the card (#32142 body and its four comments, the claim amendment included), the PR body, file list and net diff, and the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run. Check-runs on the head, all completed: 36 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, every Lint and Type Check family, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness among the 36). `origin/main` has not moved any cited file since the PR's merge base.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`AutomationEngine.registerFlow` accept-set: narrowed. Right.** A definition `FlowSchema` parses whose top-level `nodes` hold no `type: 'start'` member (an empty list included) is now refused, in every `status`. The check is one entry, first, in `registrationChecks`; `registerFlow` throws the first refusal before `flows.set`, the version history and the arm, so nothing is held. The only other writer of `flows` (`rollbackFlow`) re-seats a body registration already accepted, so no door arms the shape.
- **`POST /api/v1/automation` and `PUT /api/v1/automation/NAME`: 200 becomes `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`. Right.** No runtime change is needed and none is made: `registerAndSaveFlow` runs the engine first and answers its throw through `flowDefinitionRefusal`, whose last arm wraps any plain `Error` as a validation failure. A refused `PUT` leaves the held definition armed (the throw precedes any change). Pinned on the real stack by the dogfood file, which the Dogfood Regression Gate ran green.
- **Boot pull, `kernel:ready` bind, metadata-change sync: a stored start-less row is no longer armed. Right.** At the bind, `syncFlowsFromProtocol` warns, withdraws the name and calls `recordFlowRefusal`, and the boot completes; the mutation sync warns, keeps whatever registration the engine had, and records the refusal when it had none. The integration test pins `running`, the sibling flow armed, and the read serving the stored row beside `registration: refused`.
- **Metadata save door: accept-set unchanged. Right.** It does not run the registration checks; a start-less draft still stores and the sync records the refusal. Pinned.
- **`GET /api/v1/automation/NAME` for such a row: 200 becomes 404; metadata read: `registered` becomes `refused`. Right**, and the same as every other registration-refused stored flow.
- **Trigger doors for such a row: `422 FLOW_NO_START_NODE` becomes `404` (no flow held). Implied by the diff and NOT named.** The flipped pins assert exactly this at the engine (`execute` answers `not found`), the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet says the exit and its `422` mapping stay in place, and the published trigger table still promises the `422` for "the stored definition has no `start` node". See ④ F1.
- **Stored pass (`os migrate meta --stored`): one new TODO class at `flows[0].nodes`. Right.** It comes through the one shared list with no second change; pinned by the `CASES` row and its listing-equals-refusal agreement.
- **Region bodies and extra start nodes: unchanged. Right.** `execute()` looks for the start node in the flow's own `nodes` only, so a `start` inside a loop body never began a run; a second start node is still accepted and still named by `flow-node-unreachable`.
- **Published TypeScript and wire surface: none.** `validateStartNode` is exported from an internal module that the package index does not re-export; no spec file, error code, response shape or route moves. The consumer type gates and the liveness gate are green.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The changeset bumps `@objectstack/service-automation` `minor`, carries the BREAKING banner, both declaration lines, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). That matches what the diff publishes: the kind is `narrowed` (a requirement tightened on what an author can register), `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, and `(narrowing)` is the breaking arm. The only other package touched is the private dogfood suite, test-only, which publishes nothing. Check Changeset and the release gates are green on the head. The card-side `Clause-②: no` was amended by the seat to this spelling before this record; the two now agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0], keep `no (narrowing)`: A, answered.** The door refuses a body it accepted; no other kind is honest and the level gate accepts no other pairing.
- **open_questions[1], where the metadata save door refuses the shape: A, answered, a follow-up card for the lint lane.** A `FlowSchema` refinement would refuse a designer draft mid-edit, which is the reason `lint-flow-patterns.ts` gives for keeping `flow-node-unreachable` out of the parse. A lint rule on the runtime authoring gate refuses the live save and the publish and keeps the draft with a diagnostic. Until it lands, `PUT /meta/flow/NAME` still stores a live start-less flow and the author learns only from the read; that is the card's stated reach (MCP and AI builders write through that door) and it is not closed by this PR. The same card should correct `rule-explanations.ts`, which says on `main` that "the flow parse refuses" a flow with no start node; it does not, before or after.
- **open_questions[2], an ADR-0087 semantic entry: B stands for this head; A escalated to the spec lane as a follow-up.** The marker is gate-admitted and not self-contradictory. A precedent of the same shape exists (`picklist-binding-unknown-refused`: a door refusal with no mechanical rewrite, registered as a semantic entry), so the upgrade guide would be more complete with one. The claim forbids `packages/spec/**` here, so it cannot be this PR.
- **open_questions[3], the advisory half of the card (unknown positions, queues, channels warn at save): escalated, needs a maintainer decision.** A warnings slot on the automation write answer is a response-shape change in the spec. The PR is `Part of` and the card stays open for it; correct.
- **Deviation 1 (Clause-② spelling): accepted**, see ②. **Deviation 2 (the dogfood test outside the claimed surface): accepted.** It is the only pin of the HTTP door on the real engine, it is test-only, and it is inside this record's floor. **Deviation 3 (one commit fetched into the shared object store for a gate self-test): no contract bearing.**
- **Out-of-scope finding, `FLOW_NO_START_NODE` now unreachable: escalated to the spec lane and the lane holding `engine.ts`.** The code stays a member of the closed union in `contracts/automation-service.ts`, in the error-code ledger and in the trigger tables, while no door can make the engine stamp it, and the comment above the `execute()` exit ("is reachable from the trigger door and is not dead code") is false at this head. Retire the member or keep it as a declared defensive exit is a ruling, not a dev choice. With the pins flipped, no engine test exercises that exit any more.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the platform checklist recipe (`qa_no_start_node` through publish): confirmed.** Its own text predicted the move; its owner re-reads it.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.** I looked for a declaration on `main` that a flow with no start node does anything, and found the opposite in every place that speaks of it. `IAutomationService`'s result contract names it "an authoring defect the caller cannot fix by retrying"; the trigger table answers it `422`; `execute()` and the retry path begin a run at `flow.nodes.find(type === 'start')` and nothing else schedules a top-level node; `subflow` and `map` start a child through the same `execute()`, so a callee needs one too. `FlowSchema` accepting `nodes` with no start member is the absence of a check, which the lint docblock explains (drafts must stay saveable through the parse), not a capability. `createFlow`'s declared input is `FlowSchema`, but that door has always answered the engine's stricter verdict (cycles, regions, config keys, predicates) as a 400, and `registerAndSaveFlow` says so in its contract. So the right seat for this refusal is the registration list, not the schema and not a second call in the route, and that is where the diff puts it.

Attempts to break it, each read in the code:

- *A flow kind that runs without a start node.* None: all five `type` values dispatch through the same start lookup; a region body is a separate graph entered at its entry node; a `boundary_event` is attached to a host that is itself reached from start.
- *A draft kept through the automation door.* `draft` is enabled in this engine (`flowStatusDisabled` is set only for `obsolete` and `invalid`), so a start-less draft registered there was a live flow that failed every run. No first-party client in this repository writes definitions through `POST /automation`; the designer saves through the metadata door, which is untouched. Status-agnostic is also what every sibling check is.
- *A refused update taking down the flow it updates.* Through the automation door, no (the throw precedes any state change). Through the metadata door, the mutation sync keeps the registration the engine had (`syncMutatedFlows`), so the earlier body keeps running until the next boot, whose bind refuses the stored row; before this PR the same save replaced a running flow at once with a body that failed every run, so nothing that ran is lost.
- *A boot that fails on an old row.* No: the bind catches per flow; pinned on the real composition.
- *A stored row that vanishes.* No: the metadata read serves it unchanged beside the refusal; pinned.
- *The check reading engine state or a non-canonical body.* No: it runs on the parsed flow inside the shared list and reads `flow.nodes` alone.

Findings:

- **F1, should-fix, on the prose face (the PR body's `Skills-docs:` line; no head move).** The line reads `none`, with a reason that speaks of the skill only. The diff falsifies hand-written reference text: `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`'s trigger table row "`422` `FLOW_NO_START_NODE`: the stored definition has no `start` node", and the same sentence in `packages/client/src/index.ts`'s trigger docblocks, `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`, `plugin-endpoints.mdx` and `declarative-endpoints.mdx`. After this PR a stored start-less definition answers the trigger doors `404`, and the place an author meets the fact is the save (`400`) and the metadata read (`registration: refused`), neither of which those pages say. The docs-drift check lists nothing because no page names a derived anchor, which its own comment says is not a clean bill. Fix: rewrite the line to `follow-up owed`, naming those files, and the seat files the card; the card should also say in one sentence what the trigger doors answer for such a row now, which the changeset leaves to inference. The fix earns a delta read of the line and the card.
- **F2, nit, follow-up.** The card asks for a located refusal. The location is in the message prose and in the stored-pass site; on the wire `details.fields[]` addresses `(body)`, as every non-Zod registration refusal does. A field path needs `registerFlow` to throw its sites, an `engine.ts` change outside this claim. It belongs with the card's open remainder.
- **F3, nit, follow-up.** A start-less `api` flow now gets two stored-pass sites for one cure: the new one at `flows[0].nodes`, and, by `validateApiTriggerSecret`'s own no-start branch, one at `flows[0]`, whose words ("its start node declares no `config.secret`") presume a node that is not there. `registerFlow` throws only the first, so no door answer is affected.
- **F4, nit, accepted.** `obsolete` is refused like the rest, so a retired start-less row reads `refused` where it read registered and disarmed. Nothing ran in either case, and the sibling checks behave the same way.

No must-fix. F1 is the one item that needs an act before ACCEPT, and it is on the PR body.
